newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota wheat harvest advances to 79 percent.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota wheat harvest advances to 79 percent.

text.p: Harvesting of North Dakota's spring wheat crop continued to advance ahead of average during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop progress report.
But although overall dry conditions and above-normal temperatures allowed harvesting to proceed, they forced a decline in all late-season crops except canola.

Seventy-nine percent of the spring wheat acreage was combined versus 63 last week, 65 last year and the 68 average. Durum acreage was 52 percent combined, ahead of 33 last week, 42 last year and the average of 50 percent.
Ninety-one percent of the barley was combined versus 77 last week, 84 last year and the 86 average. Oats were 89 percent combined, ahead of 74 last week, 71 last year and the average of 79 percent.

Sunflower condition was rated 80 percent good to excellent, 18 fair and two poor. Percentage condition for other beans and oilseeds was as follows: soybeans 41, 32 and 27; canola 76, 22 and two; flaxseed 71, 24 and five.
Range and pasture conditions decreased and were rated 36 percent good to excellent, 38 fair and 26 poor to very poor.
